title: except
goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how except catches an error from try so the program can keep going.
learn: The program continues after the pair
idea: After try you write except:. If the try block hits an error, Python jumps to except and runs that code instead of crashing. When the pair finishes, the rest of the program can still run.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change friends = 0 to friends = 3 and press Run. The try path should succeed.

lines: print("That score is not a number. Using 0.")
output: That score is not a number. Using 0.

practice.text: Wrap the division in try/except. If it fails, print a friendly message. Always print Done at the end.
practice.hint: Put print(a / b) inside try:. Add except: with a kind message like "Cannot divide by zero". Keep print("Done") outside so it always runs.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if except catches the error, friendly message prints, and Done still prints.

practice.text: Try int("hello"). On failure set number to 0 and print a short message. Then print number.
practice.hint: In try:, call int(text) and store it in number. In except:, print something friendly and set number = 0.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if number becomes 0 via except and is printed.

quiz.question: When does except run?

options.text: When the try block hits an error

quiz.correct: Right, except handles the failure path.

quiz.question: Can code after try/except still run?

options.text: Yes, if the error was caught

quiz.correct: Yes, catching the error lets the program carry on.
quiz.wrong: That is why try and except help.

quiz.question: What if you omit except after try?

options.text: Python will not accept incomplete try

quiz.correct: Right, a try needs a matching except (or finally).

project.title: Safe Divider
project.desc: Set a and b in your code, with no input. Try the division, print a message in except, and then print Finished.
project.starter:
a = 20
b = 0
try:
    print(a / b)
except:
    print()
print("Finished")
